text.p: Lehman Brothers on Wednesday estimated Israel's Elron Electronic Industries would earn $0.86 a share in 1998.

"We are maintaining our 1997 EPS (earnings per share) estimate at $0.75 and have initiated a 1998 forecast calling for EPS of $0.86," analyst Ted Kundtz wrote in a report. The electronics holding company earned $0.56 a share in 1996.
Lehman maintained its 2-Outperform rating for Elron.
It said the estimates assumed Elron would realise increased value in some of its private holdings over the next two years.
In addition, Elron's results should benefit from improvement at subsidiaries Elbit Systems Ltd and Elbit Medical Imaging Ltd, Kundtz said.
The report said Elron's fourth quarter 1996 EPS of $0.19 was up 27 percent from the previous year and was higher than Lehman's estimate of $0.13.

It said it believed investors should look at Elron on the basis of the net asset value (NAV) of its holdings in affiliate companies rather than on its earnings which could vary from quarter to quarter due to many non-operating items.

Elron's shares were currently trading at roughly 17 percent premium to NAV of $11.20, Lehman said, adding it believed the current NAV understated the true value of the assets, particularly the private holdings.
Lehman estimated NAV could be worth in excess of $17 per share over the next one to two years.
